path: ServerScriptService/PlotGrowth.luau
purpose: Feature: Visible plot growth: the plot is a big empty floor, and buying upgrades barely changes how it looks. A new server PlotGrowth module listens to purchases and rebirth resets (UpgradeService already calls into Tycoon/CashInService; hook the same purchase point) and builds a themed model on the owner's plot for every owned upgrade, built from parts in the plot's PlotThemes colors and materials (never default grey), each popping in with GameAssets.popIn and a GameAssets.burst: Dropper 2/3/4 become a real dropper machine (a hopper on legs with a glowing nozzle) on the dropper row above the conveyor; Speed 1/2 add chevron arrows that scroll along the conveyor sides; ore tiers add a matching ore pile/crystal cluster beside the collector (silver, gold, diamond); Cash x1.5/x2 add a vault/coin stack with a floating 'x1.5' sign next to the collector; and after the first purchase a low themed wall with corner pillars and lamps rises around the plot edge. On rebirth all growth models are removed with a shrink tween and rebuilt as upgrades are bought again. Bump counter plot_growth_built. -- ModuleScript that owns all growth models, server-authoritative. API: `PlotGrowth.onPurchase(player, upgradeId)`, `PlotGrowth.onRebirth(player)` and `PlotGrowth.init()`. init is idempotent and is called lazily by the first onPurchase or onRebirth. It also connects Players.PlayerRemoving to clean up. It keeps a per-player set of owned growth ids and a per-player Folder named 'PlotGrowth' under the player's plot model. The plot is found through the existing plot-ownership mechanism (read PlotClaimService, PlotBuilder and Tycoon for how a player maps to a plot model, its theme name and its anchor parts such as the conveyor, collector and dropper row); if the plot is not found, warn once and return without erroring. Colors and materials come only from PlotThemes for that plot's theme (floor, accent and rail colors and materials), and no part may keep default grey. On purchase it builds the model for that id only if it is not already built:
- dropper N: a hopper (tapered or stacked parts) on four legs with a Neon glowing nozzle, placed on the dropper row above the conveyor in slot N.
- speed 1/2: a row of chevron arrow parts (wedge or arrow made from parts) on both conveyor sides. They are tagged 'GrowthChevron' with attributes for start, end, speed and direction so the client scrolls them.
- ore silver/gold/diamond: a pile or crystal cluster beside the collector in the matching ore color.
- cashmult x1.5/x2: a vault or coin stack next to the collector with a BillboardGui sign reading 'x1.5' or 'x2'.
- Wall: on the first purchase of any upgrade, a low wall with corner pillars and Neon lamps around the plot edge.
All parts are Anchored, CanCollide=false except the wall, and CanTouch=false. Each new model pops in with `GameAssets.popIn(model)` and a `GameAssets.burst` at its position (pcall-guarded, falling back to a size tween if the helper signature differs; read GameAssets first). On rebirth it tweens every growth model to scale or size 0 over about 0.4s, then Destroys it and clears the owned set. Later purchases rebuild from scratch. Bumps `ForgeTelemetry.bump('plot_growth_built')` once per model built, including the wall. Respects PartsPerModelCap. Bump ForgeTelemetry counters: plot_growth_built.

## Lessons from past builds
# Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull. Keep the second purchase within about 20-30s of idle income, by raising per-item value or lowering the price. Chain the first few upgrades so there is always something affordable to chase in the first minute, with no long dead gaps.
- Starting cash must be strictly below the first upgrade's price, never equal to it. An instant spend gives the player no chase and no sense of what cubes are for. Start slightly below the price so the first few collected cubes earn it, within about 10s. Check starter cash against the first cost in config before finishing.
- The first purchase must actually happen in a short playtest, and its counters (e.g. upgrades_bought) must be above 0. If the report lacks them, the first pad is too hard to find or reach. A highlight or "affordable" counter above 0 with no purchase counter means the pad was reachable in logic but the player never touched it. Put the first pad close to where the player stands after claiming (just off the walking path), and guide the player to it with a beam. Make sure the tutorial step that points to it fires.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases.
- Give failure feedback as well as success feedback. A pad, button, shop purchase or rebirth attempted without enough cash, or a shop card whose requirement is not owned, needs a red flash, an audible buzz, a shake and a "Need $N" or requirement toast, debounced to about 1s. Never return silently from a denied Buy handler. A silent denial confuses young players.
- Place trigger pads (buy pads, claim gates, etc.) off the spawn path so walking from spawn never fires them accidentally. They must still be easy to find and reach: guide the player to the first pad with a visible beam or arrow.
- Make moving cubes or other spawned items non-colliding with players (CanCollide = false, or a collision group) and cap their count per area. Otherwise they jitter, stick or knock players around.
- Keep the time to first core-loop activity well inside the playtest window (the probe may last only ~6-15s). Any auto-claim or auto-start fallback must fire within about 3-5s, never 20s. A spec or acceptance text that says 20s is wrong for playtests, so shorten it and keep the tested window consistent. Claim gates should sit near the spawn area, not far outside the plaza. An idle player must still reach the loop quickly.
- Budget the whole first-payout path, not just the claim: claim delay + first spawn + conveyor travel (length / speed) should land the first cash-in within about 3-4s of the claim. Use a short, fast conveyor, spawn the first item immediately on claim, and don't leave this borderline.
- Keep tutorial text consistent with the actual flow (e.g. don't say "walk to a gate" if auto-claim happens within seconds). Tutorial steps must be advanced by events that actually occur, or the player is left without guidance. Add a time-based fallback so a step can't stall. A tutorial_reshown counter above 0 means a step stalled. Give a clear objective from second 0, make the steps lead the player to every key feature (buy pad, shop), and check that the guide beam or arrow actually appears (its census count is above 0). If the census shows beams = 0, the guide is invisible: fix the beam creation (attachments, parenting, target lookup), not just its config.
- Feedback should be audible and visible: use verified sound ids from the shared asset table, not weak built-in rbxasset wavs. Add particles or ambient sparkle, and set the bloom threshold low enough that Neon parts glow.
- Shared effect helpers (burst, shake, sound, FOV punch) only matter if gameplay code calls them. Wire each helper to a real event (collect, buy, rebirth, big upgrade) and check that its counter is above 0 after a playtest. Big moments deserve stronger feedback than routine ones: camera shake, a shockwave ring, or a larger popup. The purchase is the biggest reward moment, so make sure it has a visible and audible effect and a counter. Fire milestone effects only at milestone counts, not on every event. Make the routine collect reward escalate too (bigger burst or louder sound as streaks or tiers grow), so identical feedback for every cube doesn't flatten the loop.
- Keep routine per-event effects cheap and rate-limited. One sound and one burst per cash-in, at most a few per second per player, and reuse a single Sound object where possible. Do not create a new Sound plus several emitters for every cube. Rate limits and cooldowns must apply only to routine effects. Never let them swallow milestone effects, which must fire exactly when the count hits the milestone

	return (ok and type(m) == "table") and m or {}

	if type(t) ~= "table" then return default end
	for _, k in keys do

		if typeof(v) == "Color3" then return v end
		if type(v) == "table" then
			local c = v.Color or v.color

		end
	end
	return default
end

local function asMaterial(v)
	if typeof(v) == "EnumItem" and v.EnumType == Enum.Material then return v end
	if type(v) == "string" then

		if ok then return m end
	end
	return nil
end

local function pickMaterial(t, keys, default)
	if type(t) ~= "table" then return default end
	for _, k in keys do
		local v = t[k]
		local m = asMaterial(v)
		if m then return m end
		if type(v) == "table" then
			m = asMaterial(v.Material or v.material)
			if m then return m end
		end
	end
	return default
end

local function fixColor(c, fallback)
	if typeof(c) ~= "Color3" then return fallback end
	local mx, mn = math.max(c.R, c.G, c.B), math.min(c.R, c.G, c.B)
	if mx - mn < 0.08 then return fallback end
	return c
end

local function toVec(v)
	if typeof(v) == "Vector3" then return v end
	if typeof(v) == "CFrame" then return v.Position end
	if type(v) == "table" then
		local p = v.Position or v.position or v.Offset or v.offset
		if typeof(p) == "Vector3" then return p end
		local x, z = v.X or v.x or v[1], v.Z or v.z or v[3]
		if type(x) == "number" and type(z) == "number" then return Vector3.new(x, 0, z) end
	end
	return nil
end

local function num(t, keys, default)
	if type(t) == "table" then
		for _, k in keys do
			if type(t[k]) == "number" then return t[k] end
		end
	end
	return default
end

local function scaleTween(model, from, to, t, done, style)
	local nv = Instance.new("NumberValue")
	nv.Value = from
	pcall(model.ScaleTo, model, math.max(from, 0.01))
	local conn = nv.Changed:Connect(function(v)
		pcall(model.ScaleTo, model, math.max(v, 0.01))
	end)
	local tw = TweenService:Create(nv, TweenInfo.new(t, style or Enum.EasingStyle.Quad), { Value = to })
	tw.Completed:Once(function()
		conn:Disconnect()
		nv:Destroy()
		if done then done() end
	end)
	tw:Play()
end
